items.title: One-Step Text Generation by Seq-Drifting
items.summary: This paper introduces Seq-Drifting, a framework designed to enable diffusion language models to generate entire text sequences in a single forward pass, addressing the multiple sampling steps typically required for high-quality text.

items.title: SWEAR: Section-Wise Efficient Audio Reasoning via Self-Rated Difficulty
items.summary: This paper introduces SWEAR (Section-Wise Efficient Audio Reasoning), a method for large audio-language models to achieve adaptive and efficient reasoning by incorporating self-rated difficulty for granular effort estimation.

items.title: Kairos: Toward a Byte-Level Foundation Model for Every Modality
items.summary: This research introduces 'Kairos,' a byte-level foundation model designed for every modality, featuring a novel architecture combining bidirectional gated-DeltaNet linear attention and sliding-window attention for small language models.

items.title: An Input-Dependent Readout Phase for Resonant Sequence Models
items.summary: This paper proposes an input-dependent readout phase for resonant sequence models, allowing content-dependent memory while avoiding the quadratic cost of attention. It explores trade-offs between training efficiency and memory capabilities in these models.

items.title: CacheScope: Exact-Compute Allocation for Training-Free Diffusion Acceleration
items.summary: CacheScope introduces a training-free method for accelerating diffusion transformer inference by optimally allocating compute resources to replace full denoising steps with cached approximations. The approach focuses on improving efficiency through feature reuse in diffusion models.

items.title: Transformer-Based Masked Diffusion Models Provably Learn Distributions with Latent Structure
items.summary: This paper provides theoretical proof that transformer-based masked diffusion models (MDMs) can learn distributions with latent structure, generating discrete data by iteratively unmasking tokens in parallel. It also analyzes the parallelization and estimation errors inherent in these models.

items.title: DiffusionART: Efficient, Stable and Scalable Reinforcement of Diffusion Models
items.summary: DiffusionART proposes an efficient, stable, and scalable online reinforcement learning method for fine-tuning diffusion models using black-box rewards. It aims to overcome limitations in efficiency and stability found in existing RL approaches for diffusion models.

items.title: STAPLE: Static Sparse Upcycling of Pretrained Checkpoints via Embedding Modules
items.summary: STAPLE introduces a static sparse upcycling method for pretrained LLM checkpoints using embedding modules, designed to scale parametric capacity without increasing active computation. It addresses the challenges of expensive pretraining for sparse architectures, particularly beyond Mixture-of-Experts models.

items.title: Byzantine-Resilient Federated Large Language Model via Hypergraph Message Passing
items.summary: This paper introduces a new method to make Federated Large Language Models (FedLLMs) resilient to Byzantine attacks during decentralized training, which can corrupt semantic consistency and factual accuracy.

items.title: HART: Hybrid Attention-RWKV Time series Foundation Model
items.summary: This paper introduces HART, a Hybrid Attention-RWKV Time Series Foundation Model designed for non-autoregressive multi-step forecasting, addressing long-horizon degradation seen in models like RWKV-7.

items.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling
items.summary: This paper describes an unsupervised method for training vision-language reward models without human preference labels, using a linear head on a frozen Qwen3-VL backbone.

items.title: COFFEQA: Counterfactual-Guided Few-Shot Distillation for LLM Question Answering
items.summary: This paper introduces COFFEQA, a counterfactual-guided few-shot distillation method aimed at training smaller, more efficient student LLMs for question answering tasks.

items.title: Time Delay System for Sequence Modeling
items.summary: This research proposes a 'Time Delay System' as a novel approach for sequence modeling to provide explicit, interpretable content-aware temporal recall, addressing limitations in current models.

items.title: Rethinking the Roles of Diffusion and Decoding: Predictive-State Flows for Parallel Language Generation
items.summary: This research rethinks the roles of diffusion and decoding in continuous diffusion language models, proposing 'Predictive-State Flows' for parallel language generation.

items.title: Surfing the Activation Wave: Analyzing the Information and Geometry of LLM Hidden States for Speculative Decoding
items.summary: This research analyzes the information and geometry of LLM hidden states to improve speculative decoding methods by optimally selecting layers for faster inference.

items.title: What Should SFT Learn? Conditional Information Gain for Generalizable Post-Training
items.summary: This paper explores what supervised fine-tuning (SFT) should learn for generalizable post-training of large language models, proposing Conditional Information Gain as a criterion.

items.title: RAMP: Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision for Efficient Prefill in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
items.summary: This paper introduces RAMP, a Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision technique designed to improve the efficiency of prefill operations in recurrent-depth language models, especially for long contexts.

items.title: From 2.1M Hours of Raw Broadcast Audio to Finnish Speech SSL: Confidence Filtering and Architectural Analysis at Scale
items.summary: This research details a method for creating Finnish speech self-supervised learning models from 2.1 million hours of raw broadcast audio using confidence filtering and architectural analysis.

items.title: Neurograf v1: An End-to-End Romanian-First Language Model Family
items.summary: Neurograf v1 is an experimental end-to-end Romanian-first language model pipeline, developed to assess the feasibility of training LLMs from scratch for lower-resource European languages. It includes RoSfera, a 635 GB Romanian corpus.

items.title: ForcingBooster: Adaptive Patch-wise Denoising for Fast Autoregressive Video Diffusion
items.summary: ForcingBooster is presented as a method for adaptive patch-wise denoising, designed to enable faster and more efficient autoregressive video diffusion for real-time interactive video generation.

items.title: Zebra3D: Efficient Hybrid Foundation Models For Scalable 3D Reconstruction
items.summary: Zebra3D introduces an efficient hybrid foundation model and a layerwise sparse-linear hybrid attention framework to improve the scalability and efficiency of pretrained 3D foundation models for large-scale 3D reconstruction.

items.title: APEX: Asynchronous Prefix Denoising for Extreme Compression
items.summary: APEX, short for Asynchronous Prefix Denoising for EXtreme compression, is introduced as a hierarchical method to achieve cheaper diffusion by aggressively compressing latent tokens in generative models while managing the reconstruction-generation dilemma.

items.title: UniMergeTrack: Hierarchical Model Merging for General RGB-X Visual Object Tracking
items.summary: UniMergeTrack introduces a hierarchical model merging approach for general RGB-X visual object tracking, aiming to improve robustness using complementary modalities like thermal infrared, event, or depth.

items.title: A4-MR: Abnormality-aware Anatomical Alignment for MR
items.summary: A4-MR proposes an abnormality-aware anatomical alignment method to enhance vision-language MRI models, addressing their limitations in anatomy-specific localization and pathology-aware representation.

items.title: Evolving Creatives with Clicks: CTR-Driven Advertising image Editing via Attribute Disentanglement and Preference Alignment
items.summary: This research presents a method for CTR-driven advertising image editing, optimizing e-commerce creatives by generating appealing ad images from product images using attribute disentanglement and preference alignment.

items.title: Measurable Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting with Joint Region and Depth Supervision for Interactive Building Inspection
items.summary: This paper introduces "Measurable Semantic 3D Gaussian Splatting," a 3D reconstruction method with joint region and depth supervision designed to provide geometric measurability, semantic structure, and interactive information for building inspection.

items.title: From Glance to Focus: Mitigating Recognition Laziness in MLLMs for Fine-Grained Recognition
items.summary: This research proposes a method to mitigate "recognition laziness" in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), aiming to improve their performance in Fine-Grained Visual Recognition (FGVR) tasks.

items.title: PreCoG: Preview-Edit for Efficient Video Correction in Generation-Time
items.summary: PreCoG is an iterative preview-edit method introduced to enable efficient video correction in generation-time, addressing compositional and temporal failures in text-to-video generation without requiring full regeneration.

items.title: Fix the Match, Not the Solver: STITCH -- a Self-Supervised Compatibility Measure for Eroded Visual Puzzles
items.summary: STITCH is a self-supervised compatibility measure designed for eroded visual puzzles, addressing the challenge of missing boundary regions in real-world puzzle fragments that hinder classical compatibility measures.

items.title: CompactSplat: Spatially Adaptive Gaussian Distribution for Feedforward Scene Reconstruction
items.summary: CompactSplat introduces a spatially adaptive Gaussian distribution approach for feedforward scene reconstruction, aiming to improve accuracy in recovering geometry and textures from sparse views.

items.title: High-Throughput Generative Video Super-Resolution on a Single Consumer GPU
items.summary: This research demonstrates high-throughput generative video super-resolution, achieving practical HD VSR performance on a single consumer GPU by addressing challenges in iterative sampling and spatio-temporal coupling.

items.title: Destination-Conditioned Adaptation with Semantic-Geometric Alignment for Generative Inbetweening
items.summary: This paper introduces a method for generative inbetweening that uses destination-conditioned adaptation with semantic-geometric alignment to synthesize temporally coherent intermediate frames between a start and target frame.

items.title: Golden Anchor for Video Generation
items.summary: Golden Anchor is a technique for video generation that enhances controllability in image-to-video systems by using an injected anchor image to determine key aspects of the generated video.

items.title: Evo-World: A Lightweight Vision-Language-Action Model with Future Motion Prediction via Optical-Flow Supervision
items.summary: Evo-World presents a lightweight Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that incorporates future motion prediction using optical-flow supervision to enhance robot control capabilities.

items.title: Forward Dynamics Models
items.summary: This paper discusses Vision-language-action (VLA) models and world action models (WAMs) that advance robotic policy learning by building on pretrained vision-language models and video generative models, respectively.

items.title: Beyond Actions: Learning Future Operation Targets for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: This work introduces Action--Future Coupled Effect Learning (AFCE) to extend Vision-language-action (VLA) policies by learning future operation targets, moving beyond just predicting action chunks to understand what commands will achieve.

items.summary: Wieszcz-XIX presents a 3.1-billion-word corpus of Pre-1918 Polish and introduces temporally bounded language models trained from scratch using this historical data.

items.title: MetaEncoder: Exploring the Limit of Bi-Encoders for Multimodal System One Decision Making with Natural Language Interface
items.summary: This paper introduces MetaEncoder, exploring the capabilities of bi-encoders for multimodal System One decision-making through a natural language interface. This approach focuses on outputting constrained decisions and probability distributions rather than free-form text generation.

items.title: SignRAG: Unified Retrieval-Augmented Gloss-Free Sign Language Translation
items.summary: This paper introduces SignRAG, a unified retrieval-augmented approach for gloss-free sign language translation, leveraging decoder-only large language models. It proposes a new paradigm for sign language translation that moves beyond conventional encoder-decoder models.

items.title: BioBigBird: A Sparse Attention Model for Long-Range Dependency Processing in Biomedical Text
items.summary: This paper introduces BioBigBird, a bidirectional language model pre-trained as a sparse attention model for processing long-range dependencies in biomedical text. It aims to overcome the limited context windows of existing domain-specific Large Language Models.

items.title: Prosody-to-Text: Predicting text from low-pass filtered speech
items.summary: This research explores "Prosody-to-Text," a task involving predicting text from low-pass filtered speech based on its prosodic pattern. It aims to develop a system that can generate text fitting a given prosodic input.

items.title: GHARP: Real-time Gaussian Head Animation from Large-scale Reconstruction Prior
items.summary: This paper presents GHARP, a method for real-time Gaussian head animation that generates 3D human head animations from a few input images and an expression signal. It decouples identity representation from expression.

items.title: Fluid-Gen-Zero: Grounding Pretrained Video Generators in Physics without Training
items.summary: This paper introduces Fluid-Gen-Zero, a training-free framework for physics-aware video generation of fluid-object interactions. It grounds pretrained video generators in physics by delegating motion dynamics to a simulator while preserving appearance modeling.

items.title: Omni-Diffusion-Distill: Few-Step Distillation of Unified Multimodal Diffusion Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper presents Omni-Diffusion-Distill, a method for few-step distillation of unified multimodal diffusion large language models (dLLMs). It aims to accelerate the iterative decoding process for both image generation and multimodal understanding.

items.title: Expression-Diverse References for Identity-Preserving Video Generation
items.summary: This research focuses on improving identity-preserving video generation by using expression-diverse references to better capture a subject's appearance across various facial expressions. It aims to generate more realistic videos while maintaining identity.

items.title: Transforming Image Editors into Video Editors
items.summary: This paper proposes a method to transform image editing systems into video editors, offering an alternative to end-to-end video editing by adapting existing image capabilities.

items.title: Diffusion Meta-Prompting and Steering for Generalizable Foundation Model Adaptation
items.summary: This paper introduces the Diffusion Meta-Prompt (DMP) model, a framework designed to improve the generalizability of foundation model adaptation beyond task-specific prompt learning.

items.title: No Distillation Needed: Single-Pass Real-Time Talking Heads via Acausal Noise Shaping
items.summary: This paper presents a method for single-pass real-time audio-driven facial animation for talking heads, aiming to improve efficiency over traditional diffusion models without requiring distillation.

items.title: TKCAM: Text and Keyframe to Camera Trajectory Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces TKCAM, a Text- and Keyframe-conditioned CAMera-motion synthesis framework based on generative masked modeling for generating controllable camera motion for cinematography and video synthesis.

items.summary: This paper proposes an energy-adaptive noise scheduling and whitening strategy to improve transform-domain diffusion models, addressing the non-uniform statistics of transform coefficients.

items.title: SPECTRUM: Proximal Spectral Modulation for Looped Self-Distillation
items.summary: This paper introduces SPECTRUM, a Looped Self-Distillation framework where a model learns and evolves by repeatedly generating and improving upon its own outputs for code generation tasks.

items.title: Internalizing Agent Experience into Diffusion Model Weights via On-Policy Context Distillation
items.summary: This paper proposes a method to internalize agent experience into diffusion model weights using on-policy context distillation, enhancing Text-to-Image generation by leveraging agentic prompt refinement and workflow orchestration.

items.title: Rationale-Guided Policy Optimization: Learning to Reason with Adaptive Rationale Scaffolding
items.summary: This paper introduces Rationale-Guided Policy Optimization, a method using adaptive rationale scaffolding to improve the reasoning abilities of large language models through on-policy reinforcement learning, addressing issues like reward sparsity.

items.title: Trajectory-Retrieval Speculative Decoding: When Does a Model's Own History Help?
items.summary: This research investigates Trajectory-Retrieval Speculative Decoding, a method that leverages a model's own reasoning history to improve the efficiency and quality of chain-of-thought reasoning and sequential decoding in LLMs.

items.title: QiYao-I: A Manifold Based Foundation Model for Irregular Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: This paper introduces QiYao-I, a manifold-based foundation model designed for irregular multivariate time series forecasting, addressing challenges with irregularly sampled and asynchronously recorded data.

items.title: EVFormer: An Egocentric Vision-EMG Bidirectional Attention Model for Bimanual Hand Pose Estimation
items.summary: EVFormer is a multimodal framework combining egocentric vision and EMG signals with a bidirectional attention model for bimanual hand pose estimation, intended for virtual interaction and wearable control.

items.title: Calibrated Answers About Randomized Trials From a 4-Billion-Parameter Open Model: A Registered Test and a License-Clean Release
items.summary: Fiorillo v0.5 is an open, 4-billion-parameter model released to answer questions about randomized trials with calibrated probabilities. It specializes in determining whether an intervention significantly changed an outcome after analyzing trial articles.

items.title: AccentCL: Robust Accent Classification with Incremental Expansion
items.summary: This work introduces AccentCL, a method for robust accent classification that allows for incremental expansion to new accent categories, addressing limitations in handling new data and class imbalance in speech corpora.

items.title: Quality-Aware Self-Correcting Speech Translation on an Edge Device
items.summary: This presents a fully offline, quality-aware, and self-correcting speech-to-speech translation pipeline designed to run efficiently on an edge device like a Jetson Nano without requiring retraining.

items.title: Two Vectors Replace In-Context Demos: Structured Task Adaptation via Embeddings
items.summary: This work proposes a method where two vectors replace in-context demonstrations for structured task adaptation, improving the efficiency of in-context learning in large multimodal models by avoiding repeated re-encoding.

items.title: Recurrent Looped Transformer
items.summary: This introduces the Recurrent Looped Transformer (RLT), a new transformer architecture that addresses state tracking by splitting layers between a parallel causal encoder and a recurrent decoder for efficient processing.

items.title: DLoop: Looped Speculative Decoding
items.summary: This introduces DLoop: Looped Speculative Decoding, a method designed to accelerate autoregressive generation in large language models by improving the efficiency of token proposal and verification stages.

items.title: Readout Stability in Prefill-Only Decision Models:Zero-Label Prediction and Inference-Time Compute Allocation
items.summary: This research examines readout stability in prefill-only decision models, highlighting their cost-effectiveness compared to generative language models and analyzing their inference-time compute allocation.

items.title: SanSi: A Looped Typed Decision Model for System 1.5 Thinking
items.summary: Introduces SanSi, a looped typed decision model for System 1.5 thinking that answers declared questions with probabilities in a single forward pass, bridging single-pass and generated reasoning.

items.title: APEX: Speculate smarter, not deeper
items.summary: Introduces APEX, a method to optimize speculative decoding for Large Language Models by dynamically adjusting the proposal mechanism and draft depth to reduce inference latency.

items.title: Nucleus Speculative Decoding: Plausibility-Aware Verification Beyond Exact Distribution
items.summary: Introduces Nucleus Speculative Decoding, an enhanced method for accelerating autoregressive generation that uses plausibility-aware verification beyond exact distribution for accepting drafted tokens.

items.title: Dynamic Positional Attention Modulation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
items.summary: Introduces Dynamic Positional Attention Modulation, a new Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) method for Large Language Models that accounts for attention heterogeneity across model components.

items.title: Visual Abstention in Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: Formalizes visual abstention for Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs), proposing that models should recognize and abstain from impossible visual transformations based on task rules.

items.title: Hybrid Latent Attention for Looped Language Models
items.summary: Introduces Hybrid Latent Attention, a new mechanism designed for Looped Language Models to mitigate the increased Key-Value (KV) cache size and decoding slowdown caused by repeated layer application.

items.title: DirectSpeech2LLM: A Simple End-to-End Framework to Mitigate Prompt Overfitting in Speech-LLMs
items.summary: Introduces DirectSpeech2LLM, a simple end-to-end framework designed to mitigate prompt overfitting in Speech-LLMs, enabling them to generalize better to new instructions beyond ASR.

items.title: DistScene: Object-to-Scene Distillation for 3D Scene Generation
items.summary: DistScene is a new framework for single-image compositional 3D scene generation that jointly models the environment and individual objects.

items.title: On Color Alignment in VAE Latent Spaces and Its Applications
items.summary: This research explores color alignment in the latent spaces of Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), which are crucial for text-to-image models, and discusses its applications in disentangling main factors of variation.

items.title: Compositional Concept Erasure in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Hierarchically Grounded Semantic Surgery
items.summary: This paper presents a method for compositional concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models via hierarchically grounded semantic surgery, enabling the removal of copyrighted, unsafe, or user-specified concepts without retraining the entire model.

items.title: REViT-v2: Hierarchical Windowed Roto-reflection Equivariant ViT for Equivariant Feature Extraction
items.summary: This paper proposes REViT-v2, a new hierarchical windowed roto-reflection equivariant Vision Transformer (ViT) designed for scalable and equivariant feature extraction, suitable for large models.

items.title: PhysLDM: Latent Diffusion for High-Fidelity Deformable Simulation
items.summary: PhysLDM introduces a latent diffusion model for high-fidelity neural simulation of deformable bodies, addressing challenges in long-horizon prediction for 3D volumetric meshes in computer graphics and physical AI.

items.title: Disentangling Dual Image References in Frequency Aware Diffusion Models for Personalized Generation
items.summary: This work presents a method to disentangle dual image references in frequency-aware diffusion models, improving personalized image generation by addressing text misalignment with background for text-driven image synthesis.

items.title: Unlocking Fine-Grained Perception in CLIP via Structurally-Aware Latent Masked Modeling
items.summary: This research enhances CLIP's fine-grained perception capabilities using structurally-aware latent masked modeling, addressing limitations in dense prediction tasks and the visual potential of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).

items.title: RefRoute: Decoupling Conditioning Cost from References via Compact Residual Conditioning and Spatial Routing
items.summary: RefRoute introduces a method for multi-reference image generation that decouples conditioning cost from references using compact residual conditioning and spatial routing, improving diffusion transformer efficiency.

items.title: Foveated Compression: Selective High-Resolution Preservation for Token-Efficient VLMs
items.summary: Foveated Compression proposes selectively preserving high-resolution image regions for token-efficient Vision-Language Models (VLMs), optimizing visual fidelity under fixed token budgets.

items.title: Later Is Better: Token Reduction for ViTs Under Distribution Shift
items.summary: This research shows that delaying token reduction in Vision Transformers (ViTs) improves their performance under distribution shift, recovering accuracy at a fraction of the compute.

items.title: ESP: Energy-Score Policy for One-Step Multimodal Action Generation
items.summary: ESP (Energy-Score Policy) is presented as a new generative action model, utilizing diffusion and flow matching for one-step multimodal action generation in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies.

items.title: StairVLA: Stage-Aware Hierarchical Action Generation for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: StairVLA introduces a stage-aware hierarchical action generation approach for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to improve the generation of continuous robot actions, especially with diffusion-based methods.

items.title: AMBER: Multi-View Adaptive Budget Allocation for Listwise Vision-Language Reranking
items.summary: AMBER introduces a multi-view adaptive budget allocation method to improve the efficiency and reduce inference costs for listwise reranking using Vision-Language Models in multimodal retrieval. It optimizes VLM calls by adaptively selecting candidate pairs.

items.title: DNAlign: Dynamic Null-Space Safe Alignment for LLMs
items.summary: DNAlign proposes a dynamic null-space safe alignment method for LLMs to ensure safe deployment without incurring high computational costs or degrading model fluency and factual accuracy on benign tasks. It aims to overcome limitations of existing safety alignment approaches.

items.title: Rank-Aware Speculative Sampling for Diffusion Draft Trees
items.summary: This paper introduces Rank-Aware Speculative Sampling for Diffusion Draft Trees, a method to accelerate diffusion generation by verifying inexpensive draft states in parallel. It aims to improve the computational efficiency of diffusion models.

items.title: Diffusion-Based Synthetic Data Pretraining for Enhancing Activity Recognition
items.summary: This research proposes using diffusion-based synthetic data for pretraining to enhance human activity recognition (HAR) systems. It aims to improve HAR performance for applications in healthcare and daily monitoring.

items.title: Slow-Fast Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Preservation
items.summary: This paper introduces Slow-Fast Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) as a framework to consolidate domain-specific expertise into a single student model while preserving capabilities in foundation multimodal large language models. It addresses challenges in MOPD training.

items.title: Does Every User Need a Private LoRA? Decoupling Personalization from Per-User Adaptation
items.summary: This research examines whether every user needs a private LoRA for personalized large language models, proposing to decouple personalization from per-user adaptation. It aims to improve scaling by optimizing the allocation of personalization capacity across users.

items.title: Lexicographic Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: This paper introduces Lexicographic Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation for training language models using reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR). It aims to optimize multiple objectives like correctness, reasoning, and conciseness without scalarizing rewards.

items.title: LiteEMG-FM: An Efficient and Deployable Foundation Model for Robust EMG Sensing
items.summary: Introduces LiteEMG-FM, an efficient and deployable foundation model designed for robust electromyography (EMG) sensing, addressing the variability and computational expense challenges in assistive devices and human-computer interaction.

items.title: Learning When to Commit from Partial Speech for End-to-End Simultaneous Speech Translation
items.summary: This research proposes a method for end-to-end simultaneous speech translation that teaches models when to commit from partial speech by adapting a full-utterance speech language model using prefix supervision.

items.title: Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce Sigma, the first large-scale (3B/8B) continuous diffusion language model (dLM) designed to overcome limitations of discrete dLMs for reasoning and inference acceleration.

items.title: Text-Centric Post-Training for Omni-Modal Reasoning
items.summary: This paper introduces a text-centric post-training approach to improve joint audio-visual and multi-hop reasoning capabilities in Omni Large Language Models, reducing data and training costs.

items.title: Adaptive Mutual Distillation for Balanced Multi-Task Post-Training of Large Language Models
items.summary: Adaptive Mutual Distillation is presented as a method for balanced multi-task post-training of large language models, aiming to improve performance across tasks with varying amounts of training data.

items.title: Query-aware routing for Cross-lingual performance gains in Encoders
items.summary: This research investigates query-aware routing to improve cross-lingual retrieval effectiveness in multilingual encoders for Finnish and Swedish, while maintaining strong same-language performance.

items.title: SCOPE-4D: Endoscopic 4D Geometry Foundation Models
items.summary: This paper presents SCOPE-4D, an endoscopic 4D geometry foundation model designed to improve geometric understanding for endoscopic navigation and robotic assistance. It addresses challenges in learning reliable endoscopic geometry.

items.title: FactorSplat: Appearance-Controllable Gaussian Proxies for Medical Volume Rendering
items.summary: This paper presents FactorSplat, an appearance-controllable N-dimensional Gaussian splatting proxy for medical volume rendering. It allows for region-specific intensity control beyond typical image-trained Gaussian proxies.

items.title: DAGS: Disentangled Appearance-and-Geometry Steering of a Frozen Image DiT for Temporally Stabilized Generative Rendering
items.summary: This paper presents DAGS, a lightweight, attention-free method that improves diffusion transformers (DiTs) for generative rendering by disentangling appearance and geometry steering to achieve temporally stabilized and faithful image generation.

items.title: GRAFT: Growing Agglomerative Foundation Models via Continual Teacher Distillation
items.summary: GRAFT is a method that uses continual multi-teacher distillation to consolidate the complementary capabilities of various vision foundation models like DINOv2 and SigLIP2 into a single, more capable model.

items.title: Imagine the Future, Internalize the Gist: Efficient VLA Reasoning via Internalized Spatiotemporal Imagination
items.summary: This research introduces a method for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to improve robotic manipulation by explicitly anticipating future scene evolution through 'internalized spatiotemporal imagination'.

items.title: SpectralCache: Accelerating Diffusion-Based World Models via Spectral Feature Caching
items.summary: SpectralCache is presented as a method to accelerate diffusion-based world models by utilizing spectral feature caching to reduce the substantial inference overhead from repeated Transformer evaluations during denoising.

items.title: CHASE-VLA: Post-Training Quantization Framework for Vision-Language-Action Models with Chunk-Aware Scale Estimation
items.summary: CHASE-VLA is a post-training quantization framework designed to optimize Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for low-bit inference, specifically addressing challenges posed by diffusion-based action experts.

items.title: Revisiting Visual Representation Enhancement of VLMs via Kernel Canonical Correlation Analysis
items.summary: This work explores enhancing the visual representation of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) like CLIP, which typically lack fine-grained perception, by revisiting techniques like Kernel Canonical Correlation Analysis.

items.title: SymRegFlow: Symmetry-Regularized Flow Matching for Video World Models
items.summary: SymRegFlow is introduced as a method for flow-matching-based multi-view world models to generate realistic videos with continuously varying camera poses, overcoming limitations of fixed camera rigs.

items.title: Correcting Guided Diffusion Trajectories with Spectral Alignment
items.summary: This paper proposes a method for correcting guided diffusion trajectories using spectral alignment to improve conditional image generation, specifically addressing issues with classifier-free guidance (CFG).

items.title: FiberGeoText: A Vision-Language Model for Population- Level Organization of Superficial White Matter
items.summary: FiberGeoText describes a Vision-Language Model developed for the population-level organization of superficial white matter in the brain, aiming to better characterize its complex fiber trajectories.

items.title: TRAC: Trajectory-aware Reuse and Adaptive Correction for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
items.summary: TRAC (Trajectory-aware Reuse and Adaptive Correction) is introduced as a training-free framework for efficient autoregressive video generation, improving upon existing acceleration methods for single-trajectory generation.

items.title: FUSEye: Training-Light Fisheye Detection with Overlapping Views and Zero-Initialized Adapters
items.summary: FUSEye presents a training-light method for improving object detection from fisheye cameras in mobile robots, using overlapping views and zero-initialized adapters to address challenges like radial distortion and boundary compression.

items.title: Custom Forcing: Training-Free Subject Customization for Autoregressive Video Generation
items.summary: Custom Forcing introduces a training-free method for subject customization in autoregressive video generation models, allowing users to generate videos of specific subjects from provided images.

items.title: Post-Training Frontier Text-to-Image Models by Composing Preference and Rubric Rewards
items.summary: This paper develops a post-training recipe to improve text-to-image generation models by composing preference and rubric rewards, addressing the challenge of capturing human preference with a single signal.

items.title: Rethinking Fixed Temporal Grids: Frequency-Disentangled Motion Generation
items.summary: This research proposes a new approach to human motion generation that moves beyond fixed temporal grids, using frequency-disentangled encoding to better handle the heterogeneous nature of human movement.

items.title: RYOPO: Bringing End-to-End Category-Level Object Pose Estimation into Real Time
items.summary: RYOPO introduces an end-to-end method for real-time category-level object pose estimation, improving upon existing RGB-D methods by integrating instance segmentation and pose estimation without separate stages.

items.title: OmniAct3D: Leveraging Foundation Geometry and Evidence-Grounded Reasoning for Panoramic 3D Detection
items.summary: OmniAct3D proposes a new 3D detection system for mobile embodied agents that leverages Vision Foundation Models and evidence-grounded reasoning for panoramic perception, overcoming limitations of narrow-view detectors.

items.title: ReSCUE: Re-translation with Sentence Commitment for Unsegmented Long-Form Simultaneous Sign Language Translation
items.summary: ReSCUE introduces a method for unsegmented long-form simultaneous Sign Language Translation (SLT) that uses re-translation with sentence commitment, addressing challenges in real-time communication beyond sentence-level settings.

items.title: Parasitic Co-Denoising: Unlocking 3D Human Motion Generation in a Frozen Video Diffusion Model
items.summary: This research proposes a parasitic co-denoising method to unlock explicit 3D human motion generation from frozen text-to-video diffusion models, leveraging their implicit knowledge without additional training.

items.title: Where to Look Is Not How to Fix: Pre-Denoising Diagnostics and Modality-Dependent Control in Diffusion Composition
items.summary: This study investigates compositional failures in text-to-image diffusion models by developing diagnostics and control mechanisms, aiming to understand where stress is detectable and how interventions change outputs.

items.title: In-Distribution Forcing for Long Video Generation at Test Time
items.summary: This research introduces "In-Distribution Forcing" to improve long video generation at test time for autoregressive video diffusion models, addressing issues like drifting and decaying motion dynamics.

items.title: Foresight: planning future perception in streaming VLMs without retraining
items.summary: Foresight proposes a method to enable streaming Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to plan future perception and adapt their computational pathways to evolving scene dynamics without retraining.

items.title: Behavior Pack Optimization for Video MLLM Post-Training
items.summary: This work presents a behavior pack optimization technique for post-training Video Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), aiming to improve their video question answering performance beyond relying solely on appearance and language priors.

items.title: Contextual Flow Matching: Adaptive Step Selection in Flow Models for Efficient Visual Generation
items.summary: Contextual Flow Matching proposes an adaptive step selection method for flow models to achieve more efficient high-quality visual generation, reducing inference cost without additional training overhead.

items.title: VisionMX: Unlocking Microscaling Post-Training Quantization for Vision Models
items.summary: VisionMX explores the impact of Microscaling (MX) post-training quantization on vision models, aiming to unlock efficient training and inference through low-precision elements and shared block scales.

items.title: VDOT++: Unified Few-Step Video Generation via Unbalanced Optimal Transport Distillation

items.title: Efficient Best-of-N policy evaluation for inference-time alignment
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently evaluating Best-of-N policies, a common inference-time alignment method, from logged data, particularly under sample-only access.

items.title: Tokka-Bench: Evaluating Tokenizers Across 100 Natural and 20 Programming Languages
items.summary: Tokka-Bench is introduced as an open-source framework to evaluate subword tokenizers for large language models across 100 natural and 20 programming languages using multiple metrics.

items.title: Quad-State Safety Evaluation of Open-Weight Large Language Models on Non-Canonical Inputs
items.summary: This research evaluates the safety of open-weight large language models by assessing their responses to harmful requests containing non-canonical inputs like emojis and altered spellings. items.title: sk-bench: A Native-First Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Slovak
items.summary: This paper introduces "sk-bench," a new native-first benchmark designed for evaluating large language models in Slovak, a morphologically rich West Slavic language. It comprises 30 datasets across ten skill categories, addressing the omission of Slovak in existing multilingual LLM benchmarks.

items.title: Arctic Questions, Missing Answers: A Dataset and Benchmark for LLM Abstention in Arctic Science
items.summary: This paper introduces ArcticQA, a dataset and benchmark comprising 194 questions from primary Arctic research to evaluate large language models' ability to abstain from answering when no valid option is present. It assesses their sensitivity to answer availability in scientific multiple-choice questions.

items.title: BanglaRhet: Benchmarking Classical and Transformer Models for Rhetorical and Persuasion Detection in Bangla Political Speech
items.summary: This paper introduces BanglaRhet, a new benchmark for evaluating classical and transformer models on rhetorical and persuasion detection in Bangla political speech. It aims to systematically assess model performance in a domain where only sentiment analysis has seen progress.

items.title: RELATE: An Evaluation Framework for measuring Relational Orientation of Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper introduces RELATE, a new evaluation framework designed to measure the relational orientation of large language models, particularly their impact on users' real-world relationships when providing emotional support. It addresses an under-examined aspect beyond safety or empathy.

items.title: Alice: A Large-Scale German Benchmark for Rubric-Based Multi-Dimensional Automatic Short Answer Scoring
items.summary: This paper introduces "Alice", a large-scale German benchmark for rubric-based, multi-dimensional automatic short answer scoring, designed to assess how well students grasp underlying concepts.

items.title: InsClaimBench: Benchmarking Insurance Claim Adjudication Across the Decision Chain
items.summary: This paper introduces InsClaimBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate reasoning-oriented large language models on the complex task of insurance claim adjudication, covering the entire decision chain.

items.title: Pre-training, Reasoning, Benchmarking: X-ray Report Generation on CheXpert Plus Dataset
items.summary: Focuses on pre-training, reasoning, and benchmarking for X-ray report generation in medical AI, utilizing the CheXpert Plus Dataset.

items.title: PanoPed: Beyond Bounding Boxes for Sim-to-Real Panoramic Pedestrian Tracking
items.summary: Introduces PanoPed, a sim-to-real benchmark for pedestrian tracking using full-sphere panoramic cameras, moving beyond traditional bounding box limitations.

items.title: DISRQAD: Diffusion Image Super-Resolution Quality Assessment Dataset and Benchmark
items.summary: Introduces DISRQAD, a subjective-quality dataset and diagnostic benchmark with mean opinion scores for evaluating diffusion-based image super-resolution outputs.

items.title: CLM-as-a-Judge: Evaluating an Open Contrastive Decision Model on Public Judge Benchmarks

items.title: Does Steering Break Your Model? A Multi-Dimensional Evaluation Suite for LLM Steering Methods

items.summary: This paper derives Kernelized Parameter Sensitivity Atlases (KPSA) as a new method for amortized conditional interpretability, aiming to provide input-specific information about model parameters more efficiently than gradient-based attribution.

items.title: KITE: A Knowledge-Injected Temporal Encoder for Time-Series Event Forecasting
items.summary: This paper introduces KITE, a Knowledge-Injected Temporal Encoder designed for forecasting rare, high-cost events in multivariate time-series systems by incorporating expert knowledge.

items.title: Neural expectation-maximization and meta-models
items.summary: This paper reinterprets Transformer networks as learned approximations to a hybrid probabilistic-inference procedure that combines max-product Loopy Belief Propagation with Expectation-Maximization in partially observed Markov Random Fields.

items.title: Static Gradient Attribution Underperforms a Density-Matched Random Mask on Loss-Based Forgetting Within LoRA B-Matrix
items.summary: This research finds that static gradient attribution underperforms a density-matched random mask for preventing loss-based forgetting within the LoRA B-Matrix in parameter-efficient continual learning.

items.title: NV-Tesseract-AD: Curriculum-Enhanced Conditional Diffusion for Multivariate Time-Series Anomaly Detection
items.summary: This paper proposes NV-Tesseract-AD, a curriculum learning-enhanced conditional diffusion framework for multivariate time-series anomaly detection.

items.title: REDaCT: Collapse-Free Unlearning in Large Reasoning Models
items.summary: This paper introduces REDaCT, a new method for collapse-free unlearning in large reasoning models, enabling the removal of specific information from reasoning traces and final answers without degrading model coherence.

items.title: Coordinate-Free Automatic Differentiation
items.summary: This paper proposes a new coordinate-free approach to automatic differentiation, addressing limitations of current frameworks that implicitly fix a basis of Euclidean space for defining gradients and Jacobians.

items.title: Meta-Reflective Evolution Effectively Improves Production AI Systems
items.summary: This paper introduces Meta-Reflective Evolution, an LLM-guided evolutionary optimization method that effectively improves production AI systems by addressing the limitations of existing optimization approaches.

items.title: The Expressive Power of Random-Feature MPNNs Across Graph Sizes
items.summary: This paper analyzes the expressive power of random-feature Message-Passing Neural Networks (MPNNs) across different graph sizes, addressing limitations in existing theoretical analyses.

items.title: Inverse Synthesis of Shock Time Series from Shock Response Spectra Using Ensembles of Conditional Variational Autoencoders
items.summary: This paper proposes using ensembles of Conditional Variational Autoencoders for the inverse synthesis of shock time series from shock response spectra.

items.title: Cross-Behavior Policy Optimization: Unified Learning from Offline Demonstrations and On- and Off-Policy Rollouts via a Shared Regression Target
items.summary: This paper proposes Cross-Behavior Policy Optimization, a unified method for learning from offline demonstrations and on- and off-policy rollouts using a shared regression target, improving reasoning post-training.

items.title: When Generative Models Act as Simulators
items.summary: This paper investigates the conditions under which a generative model can effectively act as a simulator, exploring their capacity to represent and allow editing of environmental states.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning via Fixed-point Flow Matching
items.summary: This paper proposes a new method for reinforcement learning called Fixed-point Flow Matching, which addresses the challenge of generating samples from complex, multimodal optimal policy distributions.

items.title: Robust Langevin Sampling under State-Dependent Heavy-Tailed Noise with Applications to LLM Fine-Tuning
items.summary: This paper presents a method for robust Langevin sampling under state-dependent heavy-tailed noise, addressing limitations in existing convergence guarantees with applications to LLM fine-tuning.

items.title: Personalized Federated Direct Preference Optimization via LoRA Adapters
items.summary: This paper introduces Federated Direct Preference Optimization (FedDPO), a method enabling privacy-preserving alignment of language models across distributed agents without centralizing sensitive preference data, addressing limitations of existing FedDPO analysis.

items.title: GIST: Generator-state-Informed Supervision for Tabular Foundation Models
items.summary: This paper proposes GIST (Generator-state-Informed Supervision), a new method for training tabular foundation models that uses intermediate generator states to reveal label uncertainty, improving pretraining beyond sampled hard query labels.

items.title: Controlled-Minimax: Stabilizing Adversarial Optimization via Control Theory
items.summary: This research investigates stability issues in minimax optimization, fundamental to adversarial learning, by modeling training dynamics as continuous-time dynamical systems and proposes a control theory-based approach to stabilize it.

items.title: Diffusion Precipitation Generation with Medium-range Weather Forecasting
items.summary: This paper proposes using diffusion models to generate daily precipitation forecasts, aiming to improve accuracy by addressing regional and intensity-dependent biases found in weather foundation models trained on reanalysis data.

items.title: Evidential Multimodal Transformers with Dempster-Shafer Fusion for Emotion Recognition
items.summary: This paper presents an Evidential Multimodal Transformer with Dempster-Shafer Fusion for emotion recognition, which robustly handles corrupted or contradictory sensor data by assigning lower confidence in uncertain situations, unlike traditional softmax methods.

items.title: Generalized Proximal Policy Optimization: Unifying LLM RL Algorithms from the Perspective of Divergence
items.summary: This paper introduces Generalized Proximal Policy Optimization, a new framework that unifies existing LLM reinforcement learning algorithms and improves upon the dominant PPO approach by allowing adaptive resistance to policy shifts.

items.title: Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL
items.summary: This paper proposes Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization to address the state distribution gap in long-horizon LLM reinforcement learning, mitigating the issue where local policy mismatches compound over autoregressive rollouts.

items.title: AutoIndexer: Flexible-Order Decoding by Training Causal Models on Chains of Edits
items.summary: This paper introduces AutoIndexer, a method for flexible-order decoding that trains causal models on chains of edits, offering an alternative to traditional autoregressive decoding which struggles with non-causally ordered data.

items.title: Contextual Correction of Parallel Draftsfor Speculative Decoding
items.summary: This paper proposes a technique for contextual correction of parallel drafts to enhance speculative decoding, a method that accelerates large language model inference by verifying multiple proposed tokens in parallel.

items.title: One Model to Loop Them All: Elastic Latent Recurrence for Language Models
items.summary: This paper proposes Elastic Latent Recurrence for language models, a method allowing a single model checkpoint to trade inference compute for accuracy by repeatedly applying a shared layer block, addressing the 'one-loop tax'.

items.title: Self-Preservation in Language Models
items.summary: This paper explores 'Self-Preservation' in language models, where models generate supplementary tasks to preserve prior capabilities during continual learning, helping to mitigate forgetting beyond explicitly provided task data.

items.title: Activating the Annotator: Operationalising Lived Experience in Data Annotation
items.summary: This research explores methods for operationalizing annotator positionality, or lived experience, in data annotation for subjective NLP tasks, moving beyond static demographic attributes to improve label accuracy.

items.title: Forecasting Corpus-Sampling Disagreement in Masked Text Reconstruction
items.summary: This research investigates how a predictor's outputs for masked text reconstruction change when using different corpus samples, evaluating it on GPT-2 vocabulary.

items.title: CliQ-RRG: Clinical-Knowledge Guided Disease-aware Visual-Textual Alignment for QA-Style Radiology Report Generation
items.summary: This paper presents CliQ-RRG, a system that uses clinical knowledge for disease-aware visual-textual alignment to automatically generate QA-style radiology reports.

items.title: BenCoDiC: A Large-Scale Contextual Cyberbullying Corpus for Bengali Political News Discourse FULL VERSION
items.summary: This paper introduces BenCoDiC, a large-scale contextual corpus for detecting cyberbullying in Bengali political news discourse, addressing limitations in existing datasets. It aims to improve robust detection and comprehensive study of harasser behaviors in online communities.

items.title: SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents
items.summary: SOAR is a new method for Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with precise credit assignment, designed to prevent evidence fabrication in search agents. It addresses the issue of agents over-relying on unreliable internal knowledge instead of external information.

items.title: PreSTO: Predictive Subtree Prefetching for Fast LLM Power Sampling
items.summary: PreSTO (Predictive Subtree Prefetching) is a technique designed to speed up LLM power sampling, which is used to improve LLM reasoning at test time. It addresses the sequential nature of PowerMH updates to make the sampling process faster.

items.title: SharP: Soft and Hard Prompt-Guided Augmentation with LLM for Low Resource Fake News Detection
items.summary: SharP introduces a method for soft and hard prompt-guided augmentation using LLMs to improve fake news detection in low-resource conditions. It addresses challenges posed by scarce labeled data in this domain.

items.title: Agreement Without Alignment: Label-Free Rubric Clarification Increases LLM-Judge Consensus but Not Agreement with Humans
items.summary: This research proposes a label-free procedure to clarify rubrics for LLM judges, which increases consensus among them but does not necessarily improve agreement with human evaluations. It aims to address disagreements in LLM-based evaluation panels.

items.title: Host-Aware Web Crawling for LLM Pretraining Data
items.summary: This research investigates host-aware web crawling strategies to optimize the collection of high-quality pretraining data for large language models. It aims to improve data selection pipelines by efficiently allocating crawling budgets across and within hosts.

items.title: Overcoming Data Imbalances with Expert Selection Biases
items.summary: This research explores overcoming data imbalances in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models for LLMs through expert selection biases. It aims to improve expert specialization during pretraining, particularly when data is imbalanced.

items.title: MoPrO-SD: Modular Prompt Optimization for Stance Detection
items.summary: MoPrO-SD introduces Modular Prompt Optimization for stance detection using large language models, addressing challenges posed by implicit opinions and sarcasm. This technique offers an alternative to fine-tuning for improving LLM performance on this task.

items.title: Towards the Roof of the World: NLP Progress in Tibetan Languages
items.summary: This paper presents the first systematic bibliometric survey of Natural Language Processing (NLP) progress in Tibetan languages. It reviews 140 publications from 2004 to 2026, highlighting the underrepresentation of Tibetan in NLP.

items.title: zip2zip++: Towards Inference-Time Token Compression with Minimal Quality Loss
items.summary: zip2zip++ introduces a method for inference-time token compression for language models using dynamic vocabularies, aiming for minimal quality loss. It demonstrates that efficiency gains from compression do not necessarily come at a fundamental cost to reasoning and perplexity.

items.title: Training User Simulators with Latent Intrinsic Feedback
items.summary: This research explores training user simulators with latent intrinsic feedback to develop LLM assistants capable of handling nuanced multi-turn conversations. It focuses on leveraging user simulation as a direct source of feedback for assistant training.

items.title: Multi-Stream Attention Residuals
items.summary: This research introduces Multi-Stream Attention Residuals (MSAR), an extension of Attention Residuals (AttnRes), which enables content-dependent retrieval over network depth by treating it as multi-head attention along the depth axis.

items.title: TraceICL: Thread-Resolved Demonstration Curation with Consistency Calibration for Robust Multimodal In-Context Learning
items.summary: This research proposes TraceICL, a method for thread-resolved demonstration curation with consistency calibration, aiming to improve the robustness of multimodal in-context learning for large vision-language models.

items.title: MIRAGE: Metric Inference and Reliability-Aware Gaussian Estimation from Feed-Forward Vision
items.summary: MIRAGE is a method for metric inference and reliability-aware Gaussian estimation from feed-forward vision, aiming to combine high-quality image-stream reconstruction with the metrically accurate motion of LiDAR-inertial estimation.

items.title: Scaling Multi-Teacher Distillation for Digital Pathology
items.summary: This paper investigates scaling multi-teacher distillation, a method for transferring knowledge from multiple teacher networks to a single student network, with a focus on its application and challenges in digital pathology.

items.title: MemReg: Streaming Outdoor LiDAR Point Cloud Registration with Hybrid Memory Buffers
items.summary: MemReg is a novel multi-frame network proposed for streaming outdoor LiDAR point cloud registration, which utilizes hybrid memory buffers to account for temporal correlations within streaming sequences.

items.title: Shift-Aware Identity-Guided Latent Refinement for Referring Audio--Visual Segmentation
items.summary: This paper proposes Shift-Aware Identity-Guided Latent Refinement, a method for Referring Audio-Visual Segmentation (Ref-AVS), an emergent multimodal task requiring precise object identification based on both visual and auditory cues.

items.title: Domain Adaptation of SAM 2.1 for Building-Component Segmentation in Image-Based 3D Reconstruction
items.summary: This research focuses on domain adaptation of the Segment Anything Model (SAM 2.1) for building-component segmentation, a crucial step in image-based 3D reconstruction workflows.

items.title: Spend Where It Matters: Particle Search with MH Refinement for Budget-Constrained Audio-Visual Alignment
items.summary: This paper introduces a method using particle search with MH refinement for budget-constrained audio-visual alignment, aiming to optimize joint audio-visual generation under limited computational resources.

items.title: Selective Spatio-Temporal Fruit Inspector (S$^2$FI): A Mamba-based Framework for Rotational Fruit Quality Assessment
items.summary: This paper presents S$^2$FI (Selective Spatio-Temporal Fruit Inspector), a Mamba-based framework developed for rotational fruit quality assessment to address challenges in post-harvest sorting for the fruit and vegetable industry.

items.title: ROSETTA: Rotation Subspace Estimation for Training-free Transmodal Alignment
items.summary: ROSETTA introduces a method for Rotation Subspace Estimation to achieve training-free transmodal alignment, enabling accurate matching of queries against databases built with different sensors or processed by distinct encoders.

items.title: MeshBind: Point-to-Mesh Binding for Non-Rigid Scene Flow Automatic Annotation
items.summary: This paper introduces MeshBind, an automatic annotation method that uses mesh models to generate per-point scene flow for non-rigid objects, crucial for autonomous driving and robotic applications.

items.title: AD-SRF: Attack-Defense Semantic Reinforcement for Multi-Modal Image Fusion
items.summary: This research proposes AD-SRF, an attack-defense semantic reinforcement framework for multi-modal image fusion, aiming to better balance visual quality and semantic attributes.

items.title: A Lightweight Velocity Correction Framework for Improving Instruction Following in Few-Step Text-to-Image Generation
items.summary: This work presents a lightweight velocity correction framework to improve instruction following in few-step text-to-image generation, particularly for complex prompts, without altering generator parameters.

items.title: JMT-YOLO: Multi-task Domain Adaptation via Segmentation-Guided Consistency Learning
items.summary: This paper introduces JMT-YOLO, a multi-task domain adaptation method that uses segmentation-guided consistency learning to enhance object detection performance across different datasets.

items.title: BLEND: Balancing Personalization vs. Generalization in Federated Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This research introduces BLEND, a new framework designed to jointly enhance personalization and generalization in federated vision-language models by integrating federated learning within VLM fine-tuning.

items.title: What Egocentric Video Embeddings Encode and How to Combine Them with Inertial Sensors for Human Activity Recognition
items.summary: This study investigates what egocentric video embeddings encode and how to effectively combine them with body-worn inertial sensors for improved human activity recognition.

items.title: UniDeblur: Unified Motion Deblurring via Fourier Convolution Learning
items.summary: This paper proposes UniDeblur, a unified motion deblurring method utilizing Fourier convolution learning to improve performance across various scenarios, cameras, and image contents.

items.title: In-Context Learning Can Help Vision-Language Models Overcome Training Priors
items.summary: This research demonstrates that in-context learning can help vision-language models overcome strong training priors, enabling them to better respond to visual evidence that violates those regularities.

items.title: Video Codec-Guided Training-Free Token Compression for Video Large Language Models
items.summary: This work introduces a video codec-guided, training-free token compression method for Video Large Language Models (VLLMs) to achieve more efficient inference by reducing visual token sequences.

items.title: MotionCoach: Constructing Multimodal Guidance for Video Professional Motion Editing
items.summary: This paper introduces MotionCoach, a method for constructing multimodal guidance specifically for professional motion editing in videos, building upon existing video editing models.

items.title: Learning Representations to Guide Pixel Diffusion Transformers
items.summary: This research investigates visual representations for pixel diffusion transformers, uncovering insights into what makes them useful for guiding generative quality in image creation.

items.title: The Evidence Anchoring Boundary: Where Visual Interventions Matter and When They Help in Multimodal LLMs
items.summary: This study investigates the 'Evidence Anchoring Boundary' to understand where and when visual interventions are effective in reducing hallucinations in multimodal large language models.

items.title: Learning Features, Not Layouts: Feature-Axis Attention as a Transfer Prior for Medical Imaging
items.summary: This research proposes Feature-Axis Attention as a transfer prior for medical imaging, addressing the unreliability of natural-image-pretrained foundation models under domain shifts and label scarcity.

items.title: Unified Generative Video Compression with Autoregressive and Bidirectional Video Diffusion
items.summary: This work presents a unified generative video compression method utilizing both autoregressive and bidirectional video diffusion models to reconstruct high-quality content from severely compressed representations.

items.title: What Visual Representations Do World Action Models Need?
items.summary: This research explores the optimal visual representations needed for World Action Models (WAMs), aiming to improve their manipulation capabilities beyond visual reconstruction.

items.title: Dataset-Specific Encoding of Image Content Underlies Cross-Dataset Failure in Brain MRI Foundation Models
items.summary: This paper identifies dataset-specific encoding of image content as the underlying cause for cross-dataset failure in brain MRI foundation models, rather than features encoding the scan's origin.

items.title: GeoGR: Spatial-Semantic Token Compression and Group Routing for Efficient 3D VLMs
items.summary: This paper introduces GeoGR, a method employing spatial-semantic token compression and group routing to achieve more efficient inference in 3D Vision-Language Models (VLMs).

items.title: Redirecting Teacher Supervision: Temporal-Response-Guided Latent Distillation for Video-Language Models
items.summary: This research proposes Temporal-Response-Guided Latent Distillation for video-language models, investigating how internal teacher supervision can further support temporal learning beyond on-policy distillation.

items.title: NOFACE3D: NOise-scheduled Focused Anchoring and Controlled Enhancement for 3D Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces NOFACE3D, a method for noise-scheduled focused anchoring and controlled enhancement, aiming to improve fine-scale detail reconstruction in 3D generation from single images.

items.summary: This research examines what visual-head discovery scores in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) actually find, investigating attention sources, necessity, and potential pitfalls in their use for steering, grounding, and interpreting models.

items.summary: LeWAM proposes an end-to-end architecture for world and action modeling using Joint-embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) to learn compact latent world models for control.

items.title: No, Cryptography Is Not “Dual Use” the Same Way AI Is
items.summary: Actor and functional application matter Originally published at AGI SurveilLance . Mainly, cryptography does one critical thing—encrypts data. It is considered “dual use” as a technology because one can employ encryption whether as a private citizen, a soldier, or a criminal. But, like a wall, it’s an inherently defensive tool by its nature. One cannot really attack with cryptography. [1] The term “cryptographic attack” refers to an attack on the cryptography of a target. [2] During the Crypto Wars , many battles were fought, but ultimately the winning side was that having public, open, ~unrestricted cryptography was the best equilibrium. In my eminently reasonable opinion, reasonable, informed people can disagree about the particular place to draw certain lines, because there are hard trade-offs and technological limits. A similar dynamic exists in the infosec community over which vulnerabilities, exploits, and offensive security tools to make public and which to keep private. Offensive security is actually a functionally dual use situation because, as with a sword, it can be used to attack or parry—the dual application is independent of the user. In the hands of a defender or security researcher, offensive tools and techniques are used to find problems so that they can be rectified, or at least mitigated, to prevent attackers from taking advantage of them in the same way. Still, certain red-teaming tools are notorious for the perceived imbalance between legitimate use by defenders and illegitimate use by attackers. Again, IMHO, reasonable, informed people can disagree on the particulars of where to draw certain lines over command-and-control (C2) frameworks on GitHub. Sword of Justice, circa 1650. (Photograph by Rama , 2017, CC BY-SA 3.0 France .) With AI, it’s the same functionally dual use situation as offensive security tooling. By comparison, nuclear enrichment is a much simpler issue, practically speaking—there’s a big divide between using moderately enriched hot rocks to boil water and using highly enriched dense rocks to create a warhead. It’s a great thing that nuclear power can be used at scale with low risk of somehow becoming a bomb. That takes a lot of extra work. [3] There’s no such divide for AI, and it’s native to the cyber domain. There is an ongoing debate in the infosec community over whether AI is “offense dominant” or “defense dominant.” I think the theoretical answer remains tricky to assess; perhaps it’s symmetrical. For now, I think the practical answer is that it is offense dominant, but that’s a whole ’nother essay. Another debate among infosec types concerns the closed-weight models from the labs—which have guardrails and monitoring, as well as specialized security versions for vetted users—vs. the open-weight models—with no, or easily overcome, limitations on use. It doesn’t help that the bulk of the best ones are made by Chinese labs. Also, the new closed-weight models tend to be released in phases, so that certain trusted entities can try to secure their products and infrastructure before a full public release. Again, whole essays. This situation makes some infosec professionals very mad. They want access to the full frontier capabilities themselves, the same as the big players. Their experience with cryptography, open-source software, and infosec leads them to the same place with AI. Open access by default; a level playing field for all. You can read one such account here: The Safety That Isn’t — Mark Atwood, Words about Thoughts There’s a legitimate gripe in there, for sure. But I have some pushback to deliver. Neither population [doomers and intelligence community alumni] has ever coordinated a vulnerability disclosure. Neither has sat on a bug for six weeks waiting for a maintainer to cut a release. Neither has weighed the risk of public disclosure against the risk of silent exploitation. They make policy for a practice they have never performed. This is plainly nonsense no matter where you come down on the arguments I described above. For one, some of the main AI labs are founded and staffed in large part by these doomers. These labs do quite a lot of basic infosec as major technology companies, even if poorly at times. For two, obviously the Intelligence Community and national security apparatus do perform a shit ton of defensive infosec work, including vulnerability disclosure. And, obviously, the doomers inside the labs, the doomers outside the labs, and the hawks inside the administration and outside it are all pretty distinct categories with conflicting views and incentives. Personally, I’m an Outdoor Doomer Hawk. The AI (presumably Claude) that wrote this under the author’s insufficiently careful prompting is … certainly not AGI. No, this author’s process is not more rigorous than mine. I’d love to see what his prompt was to make poor Claude produce such drivel. My AI would never. At no point in the essay is the issue of open-weight models discussed. Perhaps an open-weight model could have drafted his report for him. At no point is any fair, let alone charitable, interpretation offered for the opposing side(s) of this debate. The essay ends with this line: “ The word is cowardice .” I’m the kind of person that automatically tries to correct an error when I see it. Yes, I am great at parties. I have a BS-detection reflex and no patience for unearned epistemic authority. Also, nominative determinism compels me to knock people off high horses. That essay is a series of errors created by a small-minded individual lazily employing AI to produce a poorly informed, slovenly argued stance, after having a small, legitimate gripe. No attempt is made to consider alternative equilibria and their trade-offs. The wild extrapolation from the grave injustice done by Claude’s refusal to a sweeping theory of conniving doomers and hawks is breathtaking. The lack of basic awareness, inability to model the actual arguments of the other side, and unearned sense of moral superiority are awesome to behold. I think that’s a more appropriate application of “cowardice.” ^ “What about ransomware?” Think for 30 seconds about why that’s not really encryption as an attack , per se. ^ Uh oh . Seems offense dominant to me. ^ Just ask Iran… Discuss

items.title: Telephoto Camera: Pixel 10 Pro vs 11 Pro
items.summary: I'm not sophisticated enough to have noticed improvements in the main phone camera in the past 5-10 years, but distance shots are still not very good. The next generation Pixel Pro was supposed to have an improved "telephoto" camera, and when Google Fi offered me a sufficiently good deal [1] I decided to upgrade. Going from the 10 Pro to the 11 Pro the telephoto camera goes from a 1/2.51" sensor to 1/1.95", and since this is a diagonal measurement this means bringing in ~65% more light. But does it actually take better pictures? I wandered around taking pairs of pictures, all at 10x. Of this, 5x is optical zoom and the remaining 2x is cropping: I'm showing the pictures as Google Photos gives them to me. All hand-held: while a tripod would likely improve high-zoom pictures, I'm interested in real-world performance which is all going to be hand-held. Every set is the 10 followed by the 11 (taken back-to-back), cropped to 1100x1100. I started with some well lit things; here's our garden, ~35ft away: Some construction near our house, ~45ft away: A neighbor's roof, ~90ft away: Now some things that are less well-lit. These are in our bedroom with the window open for natural light but only indirect. A picture Sarah Hirsch painted, ~10ft away: Our curtains: Moving to a room with even less light, a poster on the spare room wall, also ~10ft away: There's some kind of algorithmic cleanup going on, which is especially visible in the words. Is the extra detail in the pictures from the new phone due to it doing a better job of capturing the scene, or is it just making details that look nice? Let's give it an eye exam! I made a little sheet of random handwritten letters. I could have printed a chart but I hate printers and printers hate me I expect AI-based image processing would overperform on printed text, especially in standard fonts, due to being heavily trained on it. I attached the sheet to the wall: Just like my own eyes, as the phone gets farther from the sheet it will have more trouble distinguishing the letters, and this will let us see the extent to which it looks better via real details vs made up ones. To get a sense of how hard this is, the top to the bottom of the top "g" is 7/8". Testing with eyes, at 22ft you can just barely make out some of the top-line letters but Lily and I both had mistakes, while at 11ft we could reliably read the top line letters but Lily had several mistakes on the next line. For this comparison I added Julia's phone, a Pixel 10a, because she didn't object. It would have been better to go back re-do the first part of this post, but I'm too lazy; please pass along a plausible excuse to the peer reviewers. Here's 7ft: The 10a is already struggling, which makes sense because it doesn't have any optical zoom: it's just cropping to zoom in. Looking at the letters in the bottom row, I think it's running the same image processing and just has less to work with? The letters are already getting a little unnatural in how they're depicted. The same three at 11ft: The 10a shows the "t" at the beginning of the second line as a "c", and the third and fourth lines are illegible. The 10 Pro has the third letter of the final line, "a", as "o". The 11 Pro looks noticably better than the 10 Pro, and doesn't seem to have made anything up. At 22ft: This is not what the 10a is good at, and we're no longer getting anything useful from it. For the other two this is a real test, just at their level of ability. The top two lines are right for both, but the 11 Pro is clearer. On the 10 Pro, the third line is semi-legible scribbles, and there are some misleading ones: in the third row the last four letters come out as an AI-hallucinated "i g n 5" instead of "s g a s". On the 11 Pro the third line is correct, and it's only the fourth line where it starts swapping letters. Even then, it gets 11/15 correct [2]. It looks to me like the automated cleanup is a common factor across the three Pixels, and the 11 Pro is giving the algorithms more to work with. But I also wouldn't trust any of these phones in cases where correctly capturing details at the limit of the camera's resolution was important. Overall, this seems like a nice improvement, and worth the hassle of needing to sell my old phone! [1] Google Fi was offering enough of a discount on a Pixel 11 Pro to bring the cost down below what I think I can sell my 10 Pro for. Specifically, they listed it at $1,100 with a $650 discount, bringing it down to $450 ($477 including tax), and I think my 10 Pro will sell for ~$500. The 11 Pro does have less memory than the 10 Pro (12 GB vs 16 GB, due to the AI-induced shortage ) but it still seemed likely worth upgrading for the improved camera and other smaller benefits of running a newer phone. The memory decrease isn't ideal, but looking at how I use my phone I'm not expecting to notice. [2] I read "t p o t f h p b f a g - r q p" instead of "t y a t f h p b f c g m r q p" which is four mistakes out of fifteen letters. Discuss
